Resolves #20986

Related: #20884 (the board pane joins there once #20875 lands) · #20874

The Workstation gains a second declared arrangement, **Planning**:
- **What it is:** a team schedule (`Neo.scheduler.Container`) above a release plan (`Neo.gantt.Container`) on one calendar.
- **How you reach it:** an Operations | Planning control in the top bar.
- **Its data:** seeded around today, with no network request. The schedule reads `workItems`, one provider-owned store whose records also carry the board's `status` and `order`. The board pane therefore joins by binding that same instance once `Neo.board` lands: one `createPane` branch and one item in the planning document.

This PR delivers the scheduler-and-Gantt half, which #20986 tracks. #20884's board pane is blocked by #20875 and joins in its own PR under #20884. An earlier version of this PR stayed a draft so it could resolve both halves at once. Our review flow does not pick up drafts, so the halves are split again.

Evidence: L3 (local headless Chrome on the real Workstation: its own Planning control, a pop-out into a second window, warm reloads and a cold boot, every record read back through the Neural Link with and without the Bridge) → L3 required (browser-observable ACs). Residual: AC-6, its frames taken but not yet embedded here. Residual-Owner: #20884, whose three-pane frames supersede them.

## Deltas from ticket
- **Reset to default restores the arrangement the workspace is in.** It was hard-coded to the shipped document, which with two arrangements leaves the documents and the `dock.perspective` name disagreeing. A switch is `resetTopology(name)`: one Group row carries the documents and the arrangement's name. Undo therefore returns the previous arrangement, a save records it, and the arrangement's panes come back from their windows. A tour enters through `shipped`.
- **A switch or a reset closes a window it empties.** The dock closes an emptied popup only when undo or redo replays a commit (`Workspace#projectDockCommit`), so the Workstation's Workspace takes every pane back from its windows and closes the ones a switch or reset empties. Undo re-opens them.
- **The schedule's bars read the status classes of the pane that renders them**, so a popped-out schedule keeps its status colours.
- **The shared store keeps no sorter.** `moveEvent` sorts a store that has sorters, a sort fires `load`, and a board re-projects every column on `load`.
- **Completion is `progress`.** That is the field the board's card editor writes; the schedule reads it through `percentDoneField`.
- **The release plan sits one level above the work items.** It holds phases and deliverables, on the Gantt chart's own stores as the ticket's Out of Scope keeps them, so no task appears twice with diverging dates. The plan's day is the UTC day, as in the families' examples.
- **Both panes draw on one calendar** (`view/planningCalendar.mjs`): one window from the Monday of the plan's first week, one scale, one locked width and one label format, so a date in the schedule stands over the same date in the plan. Every seeded bar is long enough for its title at that scale.
- **The e2e spec joins the CI engine tier** (`RUN_PATHS`, `ADAPTER_ELIGIBLE_SPECS`). It drives the page's own SharedWorker and passes off-socket.

- **Red first.**
  - On `a07f581f13` the e2e spec fails all 3 arms: there is no arrangement control.
  - Before the Workspace change, 7 of the 37 unit arms failed.
  - On `a07f581f13` the new unit specs cannot load, and the tour-entry arm fails.
  - The calendar arm's cut-label check reads a long title planted in a tree cell as cut, so it can fail.
- **Mutations.** The new modules were placed on `a07f581f13` with one mutation each: the store's sorter restored, the bar's status class dropped, slack seeded into the plan. 4 of 6 arms turned red, and each mutation was caught.
- **Reload order.** Reloading the opener and then the popup did not re-adopt the pane within 30 s. This is the reconnect lease the Workstation README documents, so the spec reloads the popup first.
